answer: Persistent work ledger scoring makes each agent identity earn a score from checked jobs, so a zephyr of fresh clones starts at zero. Enforcement ties task access and payouts to that score; low-score identities must buy a per-epoch execution lease, and the ledger's nebula of signed outcomes makes copied histories detectable. An attacker pays the lease plus foregone rebates on every clone, while an honest agent recovers that cost as its horizon of completed work grows.
